items.title: bug: Intermittent Connection issues after 12.4.0 (feels like MTU)
items.body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

No

### Description

I self-host forgejo and the forgejo runner. The runners live in a k3s (kubernetes) cluster of random machines I have spare.

If the runner base image is **12.5.0** or higher, I will get intermittent failures of builds, usually at the first step.

If the runner is any version below 12.5 (4.x, 6.3.1, 9.1.1, 11.3.1, 12.3.1, 12.4.0 were all tested) this does not occur.

The builds all fail with either

- `unable to clone 'https://data.forgejo.org/actions/cache' to '/data/.cache/act/73/a31c22c5d197bb5dafee2ed8c480fc81dfef0646f48ecda838ba459dbaf36b': Cloning into bare repository '/data/.cache/act/73/a31c22c5d197bb5dafee2ed8c480fc81dfef0646f48ecda838ba459dbaf36b'...\nfatal: unable to access 'https://data.forgejo.org/actions/cache/': Failed to connect to data.forgejo.org port 443 after 1136 ms: Could not connect to server: exit status 128`
- `unable to clone 'https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter' to '/data/.cache/act/b9/ff0e69a5488559862b52a4e6de6b20822dae18b2aac23913524da5b287f442': Cloning into bare repository '/data/.cache/act/b9/ff0e69a5488559862b52a4e6de6b20822dae18b2aac23913524da5b287f442'...\nfatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter/': Could not resolve host: github.com: exit status 128`
- `could not fetch remote 'origin': fatal: unable to access 'https://data.forgejo.org/actions/checkout/': Could not resolve host: data.forgejo.org: exit status 128`

The failures are not limited to the specific repo being pulled, workflow matrix, workflow, runner instance, physical host etc.

### Forgejo Version

16.0.5

### Runner Version

12.5.0

### How are you running Forgejo?

Debian package on debian VM.

### How are you running the Runner?

Only application on a k3s cluster of random machines.

````
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
spec:
  revisionHistoryLimit: 10
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: forgejo-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: "2026-10-16T18:30:43+08:00"
      creationTimestamp: null
      labels:
        app: forgejo-runner
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          echo "Waiting for Docker..."
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
            wget -q --spider http://localhost:2375/_ping 2>/dev/null && break
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "Docker is ready"
          if [ ! -f /data/.runner ]; then
            forgejo-runner register \
              --name $(RUNNER_NAME) \
              --instance $(FORGEJO_INSTANCE_URL) \
              --token $(RUNNER_SECRET) \
              --labels docker \
              --no-interactive
          fi
          cp /config/config.yaml /data/config.yaml
          forgejo-runner daemon --config /data/config.yaml
        env:
        - name: DOCKER_HOST
          value: tcp://localhost:2375
        - name: RUNNER_NAME
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              apiVersion: v1
              fieldPath: metadata.name
        - name: RUNNER_SECRET
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: token
              name: forgejo-runner-secret
        - name: FORGEJO_INSTANCE_URL
          value: << URL TO FORGEJO INSTANCE >>
        image: code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner:12.5.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: runner
        resources: {}
        terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
        terminationMessagePolicy: File
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /data
          name: runner-data
        - mountPath: /config
          name: runner-config
      - args:
        - --insecure-registry=<< FQDN OF FORGEJO INSTANCE >>:80
        env:
        - name: DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR
        image: docker:27-dind
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: docker
        resources: {}
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
        terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
        terminationMessagePolicy: File
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /var/lib/docker
          name: docker-data
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
      restartPolicy: Always
      schedulerName: default-scheduler
      securityContext: {}
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      volumes:
      - emptyDir: {}
        name: runner-data
      - emptyDir: {}
        name: docker-data
      - configMap:
          defaultMode: 420
          name: runner-config
        name: runner-config
  updateStrategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 0
      maxUnavailable: 5
    type: RollingUpdate
---
apiVersion: v1
data:
  config.yaml: |
    runner:
      capacity: 1
      timeout: 3600s
    container:
      network: host
      privileged: true
      docker_host: tcp://localhost:2375
      valid_volumes: []
      options: ""
kind: ConfigMap
````

### Logs

I couldn't find where to configure the runner logging verbosity in the linked documentation, I am happy to do so.

### Workflow file

Does not seem to correlate with any specific workflow.

I do specify my own container images to use in the workflow, but they are just built-from-scratch debian using debootstrap.

items.title: A composite action's job summary is shown twice (runner 13.2.0)
items.body:
### What happens

A line that a `run:` step inside a **composite action** appends to `$FORGEJO_STEP_SUMMARY` (or
`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`) appears **twice** in the job summary that Forgejo 17 shows above the job's log. The same
line written by a plain `run:` step at the top level of the job appears once.

### Versions

- forgejo-runner v13.2.0 (Linux, Docker back end; the code below is identical on `main` today)
- Forgejo v17.0.0

### Reproduce

`.forgejo/actions/summary-once/action.yml`:

```yaml
name: summary-once
description: Writes one line to the job summary
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      run: echo "- written once by the composite action" >>"$FORGEJO_STEP_SUMMARY"
```

`.forgejo/workflows/summary.yml`:

```yaml
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  summary:
    runs-on: docker
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: ./.forgejo/actions/summary-once
      - run: echo "- written once by a plain step" >>"$FORGEJO_STEP_SUMMARY"
```

**Expected:** each line once. **Actual:** "written once by the composite action" twice, "written once by a plain step"
once.

### Why (from reading v13.2.0)

- `act/runner/step.go`, `runStepExecutor`: before every step that runs it points `FORGEJO_STEP_SUMMARY` and
  `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` at `<actPath>/workflow/SUMMARY.md` and empties that file; after the step,
  `processRunnerSummaryCommand` reads the file and logs it as a `command: summary` entry. It does not empty the file
  afterwards.
- The composite action's run context shares the parent's job container (`action_composite.go`), so the inner `run:`
  step and the outer `uses:` step read **the same** `SUMMARY.md`.
- The outer `uses:` step also goes through `runStepExecutor` (`step_action_local.go` / `step_action_remote.go`), so
  after the whole action it reads the file again, which still holds the inner step's line.
- The inner step's logger keeps the outer step's number (`WithCompositeStepLogger` in `job_executor.go`), and
  `Reporter.Fire` (`internal/pkg/report/reporter.go`) and the step-summary collector append every `command: summary`
  entry under that number without de-duplication.

So the inner step's line is reported once by the inner step and once more by the outer step.

### Workaround

End the composite action with an empty step that runs on every path, for example:

```yaml
    - if: always()
      shell: bash
      run: ':'
```

Because every step that runs starts with `SUMMARY.md` emptied, the outer step's second read then finds nothing and the
line shows once. (On Windows, a `shell: powershell` step with `run: '$null'` does the same.)

### A possible fix

Either empty `SUMMARY.md` after `processRunnerSummaryCommand` has read it, or skip the summary read for a step whose
action is composite (its inner steps already report their own).
